what_it_does: Training large AI models on many chips at once requires constantly deciding how to split each mathematical operation — for example, a giant multiply of two large tables of numbers — across the available chips so they finish as fast as possible while not overloading the connections between them. This is called intra-operator parallelism: chopping a single operation into pieces and farming those pieces out in parallel. The ASPLOS/EuroSys 2025 contest challenged competitors to write algorithms that find the best such split strategy for a set of representative AI operations on a simulated cluster of accelerator chips. This paper describes the contest itself: the benchmark design, the rules, the algorithmic challenges (the number of possible ways to split an operation grows explosively with chip count), and a retrospective analysis of how top teams approached the problem. It is primarily a contest report rather than a new technical contribution, based on the abstract alone.
